## Recommended Chunk Size and Overlap for text-embedding-3-small in Document-QA RAG

For a typical document-QA RAG pipeline using `text-embedding-3-small`, the most widely cited recommendation is **1,000 tokens per chunk with a 200-token overlap (20%)** [1]. This configuration balances sufficient context for meaningful embeddings against the computational cost of generating and storing them, and sits well within the model's 8,191-token maximum context window [3].

### Why These Numbers

Token-based chunking is preferred over character-based splitting because `text-embedding-3-small` processes text as tokens using the `cl100k_base` encoding [4]. A 1,000-token chunk is large enough to capture coherent ideas from a paragraph or section while remaining small enough to keep retrieved passages focused and relevant to user queries [1]. Chunks that are too large introduce noise; chunks that are too small lose surrounding context and produce less useful embeddings [5].

The 200-token overlap ensures that sentences or concepts split across chunk boundaries are still represented in at least one chunk, preventing retrieval gaps at seams [1].

### Practical Splitting Approach

Splitting should follow logical text boundaries rather than hard token counts. Recursive character splitting using separators like `"\n\n"`, `"\n"`, and spaces is recommended so that paragraphs and sentences remain intact wherever possible [1]. This preserves semantic coherence within each chunk.

### Alternative Guidance

Some sources suggest a slightly smaller default of **400–512 tokens with 10–20% overlap** as the best starting point for general RAG use cases, noting that this range offers strong retrieval precision, particularly for shorter, denser documents [7]. The right choice ultimately depends on document type and query patterns — for paginated PDFs, page-level chunking has shown strong benchmark performance, while semantic chunking can improve recall by up to 9% at higher computational cost [7].

### Summary

| Parameter | Recommended Value |
|---|---|
| Chunk size | 1,000 tokens (or 400–512 for denser docs) |
| Overlap | 200 tokens (~20%) |
| Splitting method | Recursive, boundary-aware |
| Encoding | cl100k_base |

For most document-QA pipelines, starting at 1,000 tokens / 200-token overlap [1] and adjusting based on retrieval quality is a sound approach.
